title: Subproject workflows and native capabilities
summary: Desktop and Android share direct project, subproject and stage navigation with small host summaries. Before-first-message completion changes drafts only; editable workflows retain the existing execution and native setting authority.

chapters.title: Drafts and conversations
chapters.summary: General chats and subprojects are peers in direct navigation; metadata summaries preserve lineage without loading editable graph or conversation content.

chapters.title: Native PC capabilities
chapters.summary: Zero-turn discovery and explicit native changes expose disabled state, stable scope and durable recovery.

chapters.title: Frozen execution
chapters.summary: Graph preparation feeds the existing ledger and managed attempts while keeping current draft edits independent.

nodes.label: Shared project and conversation tree
nodes.detail: General chats and subprojects are peers. Stage chats open by stable Session ID; tree, recent and title search share one projection and host-scoped view state.

evidence.claim: One metadata-only projection keeps chats and subprojects as peers, attaches stage conversations by exact links, folds subagent chats under their parent with what they need, and adds a worktree level only when one is active.
Host-scoped view state preserves search, expansion and selection. Scroll restoration waits for asynchronous row height; chevron expansion and named-item opening remain separate.
Android derives a nonsecret authority fingerprint and uses the same shared navigation projection for the connected host.

nodes.label: Before-first-message discovery
nodes.detail: Selection discovers metadata before the first message. Skills and commands edit the current draft; /resume opens history without submitting a model turn.

evidence.claim: Discovery begins when provider/workspace/session scope changes, before a message, and rejects stale asynchronous results after navigation.

The shared controller keeps the keyboard-selected option in the completion list, preserves draft context, respects IME composition, offers @ workspace files where the host can search, and runs history and app commands without submitting.

Suggestions distinguish application actions (history, plan, model, new conversation, start over in place) from native skills; insertion replaces only the current token and preserves other draft fields.

nodes.label: Workflow draft authority
nodes.detail: Host-scoped revisioned drafts preserve stable node IDs, change history, archive boundaries and user ownership.

evidence.claim: One serialized host boundary validates project/host/revision and exact receipts. AI may edit graph drafts and prepare, start, pause, resume or cancel runs, but cannot approve, integrate, archive, change ownership or set auto-approve.

nodes.label: Native capability authority
nodes.detail: Reviewed providers share PC configuration. Android manages that PC through authenticated v14 calls.

evidence.claim: The reviewed provider supplies native metadata; built-in workflow skill appears only when tools are bound. Stable revisions include native configuration identity and host scope.

nodes.label: Saved stage references
nodes.detail: Host-resolved snapshots keep document and accepted-result references stable until the user refreshes them.

evidence.claim: Stage writes follow exact saved lineage, including continuation sources. Archived or removed stages block sending; context uses immutable saved references until an explicit refresh.
Explicit continuation copies the original stage reference snapshot after checking project, ordinary Session ownership and active stage; it does not silently refresh references.

nodes.label: AI draft and preview tools
nodes.detail: Ordinary sessions can edit authorized drafts or one bound creation preview. Preview edits cannot create a saved subproject; run start and approvals require a user command.

evidence.claim: Session-authorized workflow tools read, validate, preview and edit drafts, and run flows and read their results, through the same host service; caller project identity cannot retarget the capability.

One serialized project boundary binds a creation preview to one ordinary conversation. Exact command receipts and monotonic revisions reject duplicate contents, discarded-preview replies and changed drafts.

nodes.label: Durable native change receipts
nodes.detail: Unknown outcomes block new mutations across process restarts. Receipt inspection never reruns native work.

evidence.claim: Native mutation saves an uncertain receipt before work, checks current revision and scope, never repeats the same command, and exposes nonsecret restart recovery plus explicit acknowledgement.

nodes.label: Frozen graph and run preparation
nodes.detail: Explicit user preparation captures a graph revision and scoped planning baseline in the existing SQLite execution ledger.

evidence.claim: User or project-agent run commands freeze graph, scoped planning and auto-approve policy into the ledger; agents cannot approve or integrate; receipt fingerprints reconcile retries before preparation or dispatch.

nodes.label: Verified graph execution
nodes.detail: Conditions, parallel joins, retry limits and approval waits advance only from verified frozen-run evidence.

evidence.claim: Runtime projection reads only the frozen graph and verified outcomes. Conditions, parallel joins, bounded retries and user approvals govern stage activation.

nodes.label: Managed provider attempts
nodes.detail: Existing worktree, permission, independent-review and integration gates remain authoritative for stage execution.

evidence.claim: Provider attempts retain deterministic identities and managed worktrees while receiving only verified predecessor outputs selected by the frozen activation.

nodes.label: Native Codex and Claude
nodes.detail: Native metadata is separate from model submission; selected skills and user settings follow provider-specific supported protocols.

evidence.claim: Codex metadata uses model, skill, installed-plugin, MCP-status and cwd-specific config RPCs without thread or turn creation; disabled state and native scopes are distinct.

Claude discovery starts an ephemeral empty-input SDK query with native setting sources, reads models/commands/MCP and CLI plugins, then closes it without submitting a prompt; concurrent callers for one folder share that launch.

nodes.label: Small navigation summaries
nodes.detail: The host returns names, stage archive state and Session links. The list receives no graph instructions, documents, run bodies or transcripts.

evidence.claim: The navigation service caches a revisioned metadata projection with subproject titles, stage names and deduplicated Session links, including each run's stage and review agents under their stage.
Lazy metadata reads are fenced by host identity and coalesced per project; pagination remains separate and visible navigation polls only lightweight workflow summaries.
